intro: This playbook turns the atlas into a plan for the 16 days from Sun 11 Oct to election day on Tue 27 Oct. Field work is a margin lever. A realistic programme of 150,000 to 400,000 completed contacts is worth about 900 to 2,000 net votes for a change-led government, or about 1,500 to 2,600 under the deny-61 objective. That adds +0.05 to +0.1 points to the chance of a change-led government. It still matters: in 2022 the blocs finished about 30,000 votes apart and Meretz missed the threshold by 4,061 votes. The evidence favours three things: identify supporters this week, contact them in person in the final ten days in polling-station areas where extra turnout nets change-bloc votes, and protect the vote on election day. Rescue of votes headed below the threshold is a media and insurance programme timed to the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct, plus calls to identified voters. Persuasion across blocs is small this late: the atlas assumes about 3 switchers per 1,000 conversations with soft Netanyahu-bloc voters.

timeline.title: Decide, identify supporters, test messages
actions: Leadership decisions this week: how much weight to give the deny-61 objective, the Arab-sector policy (through election counsel), and whether to commission a Druze poll or list check before any work in Druze towns.

Cut walk and call lists only from polling-station areas the atlas scores as positive, and send door teams only where at least 1,000 contacts are available. Start with the turnout engines: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Haifa, Ramat Gan, Rishon LeZion, Herzliya, Holon, Rehovot, Kfar Saba and Givatayim.
Field-check very low-turnout stations before sending teams. Many registered voters live abroad or elsewhere, as in central Eilat and the Netanya hotel strip.
Run supporter ID by volunteer phone and door. Record the registered address and polling station, household members, list preference and how sure each supporter is to vote.

In supporter-list ground (Jerusalem, Netanya, Bat Yam, Be'er Sheva, Hadera, Eilat, Tiberias, Dimona), identify supporters by phone and relational asks only. Most voters there back the Netanyahu bloc, so the value lies with identified change supporters.
Split turf between the four lists by each station's lead change list (see 'Four lists, one street').
Build call lists of identified Blue and White and Reservists supporters for the rescue programme. Do not send door teams after them.
Test Oct 7 accountability, equal burden, cost of living and unity frames on online panels before buying media.

Aim persuasion at identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters, with right-credentialed messengers. Petah Tikva is the atlas's persuasion battleground, and persuasion value is also high in Rishon LeZion, Jerusalem, Holon and Netanya.
Recruit relational organisers. Each volunteer lists 10 to 20 friends and relatives registered in target localities.
Ask every young supporter where they are registered, and recruit volunteers on campuses.

timeline.title: Surplus-agreement deadline; first ID pass done
actions: Surplus-agreement filings close today. Signed so far: Likud-RZP, Together-Yisrael Beytenu and Yashar-Democrats. Expected: Shas-UTJ, Otzma-Amcha and Joint List-Ra'am. Likud signed with RZP and not with Otzma.
This is a leadership and legal task, not a field one. Confirm with election counsel that the change lists' filings are complete.
Close the first round of message tests and lock the frames for scripts and paid media.
Finish the first supporter-ID pass in the turnout engines. Shabbat starts this evening, so schedule Saturday-night door shifts.

timeline.title: Turnout contact peaks
actions: Switch volunteers from ID to vote plans. Live calls in the final 7 to 10 days work best. In one US test, calls in the first three weeks of a month-long drive had no effect, though another study found early calls can also work.
Ask the vote-plan questions (when, which polling station, with whom) in every live contact.

Stack several contacts on identified supporters who are unsure they will vote, in positive-value stations. Give priority where resident turnout was about 30-55%, where the atlas's turnout effect peaks. Effects roughly add up across contacts, with no extra synergy. They spill over within households but not to neighbours, so plan by household.
In supporter-list ground, call and message identified supporters only.
Prepare the rescue programme: tested insurance creative for digital and media, and call scripts for identified Blue and White and Reservists supporters. Hold the main push for Thu 22 and Fri 23 Oct.
Start the paid persuasion flight around 21 Oct, on tested creative only. Ad effects fade within days.
Confirm trip plans with students and young adults registered at a parent's address.

No change-bloc-run, funded or branded turnout work in Arab localities. Any Arab-sector support is a leadership decision, and it must be independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel in writing.

timeline.title: Final published polls; rescue peaks
actions: This is the last day polls may be published. The publication ban starts at the end of Friday and runs to the close of polls on Tue 27 Oct.

Run the rescue and insurance push around today's final polls: digital and media messages, plus calls to identified Blue and White and Reservists supporters. Insurance voting follows polls that show a list below the threshold and a clear coalition path.

Speak to Reservists voters with respect, through reservists, about threshold arithmetic. Leadership decides first whether to target them at all, because rescuing Reservists votes cuts against the deny-61 objective.

Expect late consolidation on the right. In 2015 Likud won 30 seats against 20-23 in the final polls, about 7-10 seats more, consistent with late switching from smaller right-wing lists, though poll error may explain part of it.

Check allies' threshold odds after the final polls. In the forecast the Democrats pass in 98% of simulations, Yisrael Beytenu in 97% and Together in 99%. If any slips, switch insurance messaging to protect it.
Shabbat starts this evening. Schedule Saturday-night door shifts in positive-value turf.

timeline.title: Blackout weekend: final contacts
actions: No new polls may be published from Sat 24 Oct until the polls close. Rescue messages now rest on Friday's published numbers. Do not publish, post or leak internal polls.
Send one or two SMS reminders to supporters in this window. In one Danish experiment, texts sent before election day beat texts sent on the day, and extra texts added nothing.
Release the relational asks. Supporters message their own friends and relatives from their own phones.
Run door shifts on Saturday night, Sunday and Monday in positive-value turf, and reconfirm each vote plan.
Expect threat-framed late messages from the Netanyahu bloc about who is voting, as in 2015. Answer with positive reminders to our own supporters, never with messages about other groups' turnout.
Brief call teams, polling-committee members, observers and lawyers. Free intercity buses (routes over 15 km) and all trains run from 20:00 on Mon 26 Oct.

timeline.title: Bank the vote early, then chase laggards
actions: Election day is a statutory holiday. In 2022 most polls ran 07:00-22:00 (08:00-20:00 in small communities); confirm the 2026 hours with the CEC.
Bank identified change-bloc supporters early through private contact (calls, texts, relational asks). Make no public turnout claims.
Expect the first CEC releases to show high turnout in change-bloc areas, and Likud to use them. Have the counter-message to our own supporters ready before 10:00.
After each CEC station-turnout release (at least four), rank positive-value target stations by how far they trail and move callers there.
Parties cannot be told who has voted. Callers ask identified supporters in lagging stations whether they have voted yet.
Committee members and observers stay in contested and mixed stations, and lawyers stay on call all day. No rides, gifts or activity near polling stations without clearance from election counsel.

timeline.title: Count, double envelopes, evaluation
actions: Regular stations report first. Double-envelope ballots (soldiers, hospital patients, prisoners, diplomats and others) are counted centrally afterwards. There were 462,807 in 2022, close to 10% of votes cast.
Do not call threshold races on the regular count. Ra'am and RZP-Zehut each pass in about 78% of simulations.
Keep observers on the count, including the central double-envelope tally where the law allows, and keep lawyers on call until the final result.

Compare worked and unworked polling stations in the official results to measure what the field programme did. The forecast gives a repeat election a 41.9% chance, and the next campaign will need these estimates.

tactics.effect: No direct effect on turnout. It makes every list programme possible. In the atlas, identifying 30% of supporters lifts a 150,000-contact programme from 935 to 1,207 net votes and a 400,000-contact programme from 1,607 to 1,995 (change-led government). Budget the ID contacts needed to build the lists on top of that.
tactics.israel: Run it now, by volunteer phone and door. Parties cannot learn on election day who has voted, so pre-identified supporters are the only basis for chasing. Likud says limits on the Elector app force it into more manual work. Record registered address and station, household, list preference and certainty to vote. In supporter-list ground (Netanyahu-majority towns with many change voters), identify by phone and relational asks only.

tactics.effect: Atlas value: a 1.5-point turnout lift per completed conversation at the reference baseline. The atlas scales this by resident turnout (x1.5 at 30%, a peak of x1.8 near 42%, x1.2 at 55%, x0.7 at 65%, x0.4 at 75%, x0.22 at 85%), then applies a x1.3 household multiplier. Evidence: US high-salience 3.05 pp [1.20, 4.90]; European pooled 0.78 pp [-0.16, 1.71]; US effects are largest where control-group turnout is 30-50%. In two-voter households about 60% of the effect reaches the second voter. Persuasion add-on: about 0.3% of contacted soft Netanyahu-bloc voters switch.
tactics.israel: Knock only in positive-value station areas, at no more than 35% of the resident roll, and only where at least 1,000 contacts are available. Send volunteers, not candidates: in Italy volunteers raised turnout 5.0 pp and candidates -0.4. Contact rates behind building intercoms are unknown, so log every attempt and recalibrate weekly. In mixed-bloc households keep the message about voting itself; in a UK phone experiment, partisan mobilisation spread more in politically mixed households. Druze towns score highest per contact, but their 2026 vote depends on which Druze candidates the lists field. Send no outside volunteers there; any work is led by local Druze figures on the lists, after a poll or list check. The atlas halves capacity in 49 localities within 5 km of Lebanon and 40 within 7 km of Gaza.

tactics.effect: Planning value about 1 pp per completed call. US high-salience estimate 2.28 pp [1.12, 3.43]; eight US volunteer campaigns gave 3.8 pp among those reached. Typically 10-12% of numbers dialled complete.
tactics.israel: Use it for supporter-list ground and for voters the canvass misses: young people registered at a parent's address, dispersed rural supporters, and Russian speakers through in-language callers from the community. ID calls until 16 Oct, vote-plan calls from 17 Oct, and calls to identified supporters in lagging stations on election day.

tactics.effect: One US trial (2018 midterms) found 8.26 pp [1.2, 15.3] among people messaged because of the treatment and 2.09 pp across everyone targeted, at 76-79% baseline turnout. Fewer than a third of intended targets actually got a message. The same paper's benchmark for automated texts is 0.44 pp.
tactics.israel: Israel's dense family and WhatsApp networks suit it. Each volunteer and committed supporter lists 10-20 friends and relatives registered in target localities and messages them personally in the final three days. Parties may receive the voter register but may not pass it to third parties, and in 2020 a flaw in Likud's Elector app exposed the records of about 6.5 million adults. Keep any register matching inside the party and confirm privacy rules with election counsel. The effect rests on one study, so A/B test it internally.

tactics.effect: Plan-making raised turnout 4.1 pp among those reached, against -0.2 for a standard call, and the whole effect came from single-voter households (9.1 pp). Replications are mixed: a mailer gave 0.5 pp, and two phone replications were null.
tactics.israel: Ask when, at which polling station and with whom in every live contact from 17 Oct. Voters can vote only at the station of their registered address. Young singles and older people living alone gain most. Intercity buses on routes over 15 km and all trains are free from 20:00 on 26 Oct. The announcement does not cover city buses, so plan for local fares.

tactics.tactic: Rescue and insurance messaging (media, digital, calls to identified voters)
tactics.effect: Atlas assumption, without experimental support: 5% of contacted Blue and White or Reservists voters move to a viable list, 60% to change lists and 40% to Likud. At saturation that is worth 286 net votes for a change-led government and 1,014 for change-bloc seats, and -186 under the deny-61 objective. Evidence: insurance voting depends on polls showing a list below the threshold and on clear coalition signals; coalition considerations decided about 1 in 10 Israeli votes in 2003.
tactics.israel: Blue and White polls about 0.6% (pass chance 1%) and Reservists about 1.6% (20%). An extra vote for either is worth close to zero for a change-led government, against about 0.5 pp per 10,000 votes for Yashar, Together or the Democrats. Rescue voters are about 2% of a station's voters, so use media, digital and calls to identified supporters, not door teams. Time it around the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct. Respect both lists, their leaders and reservists' service, and talk about threshold arithmetic. See 'Rescue and insurance'.

tactics.effect: Cold texts 0.22 pp per targeted voter in high-salience US races; warm texts to opted-in supporters 0.68 pp [0.05, 1.41]. Danish pooled 0.74 pp, and extra messages to the same person added nothing. In one of the Danish experiments, texts sent before election day beat texts sent on the day.
tactics.israel: Send one or two texts to identified supporters in the 1-3 days before 27 Oct. In a higher-salience US election casual voters responded and habitual voters did not, so aim at supporters who are unsure. Check bulk-messaging and privacy rules with election counsel.

tactics.effect: About 0.74 pp per completed call in high-salience US races. Low-quality vendors about 0.2 pp, high-quality ones 0.9-1.4. A chattier script beat a standard one (3.4 vs 1.2 pp) in a US commercial phone test, and in another test only final-week calls worked. Robocalls have no high-salience estimate.
tactics.israel: Buy only extra capacity for the final week, from a high-quality vendor using a conversational script and the vote-plan questions. Skip robocalls.

tactics.effect: US social-pressure mail gave 1.38 pp in high-salience races. Gratitude mailers gave about 2.4-2.5 pp in lower-salience races, about two-thirds of the effect of the mailer showing a voter's own history. A partisan version of that mailer had no effect.
tactics.israel: Parties cannot be told on election day who has voted. Whether vote-history data may be used before election day is unclear. Send no message that refers to a voter's own past turnout without written clearance from election counsel. Use gentle, unbranded descriptive norms and thanks in texts and scripts. No shaming.

tactics.effect: Peer-reviewed attitude effects are durable but small (d 0.04-0.08), and argument-only conversations had no effect. The only vote-choice estimate (3.1 net votes per 100 conversations) is a sponsor release. Conversations are long, so each one costs more volunteer time than a standard contact.
tactics.israel: Use trained volunteers with identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters where the atlas shows persuasion value: Petah Tikva first, then Rishon LeZion, Jerusalem, Holon and Netanya. Listen first. An Israeli field study found that messages exaggerating hawkish views, without challenging them, made attitudes more conciliatory for up to a year; its vote effect was self-reported. Judge the tactic per volunteer-hour.

tactics.effect: No turnout effect. It protects the count and helps deal with intimidation. In April 2019 a Likud-funded contractor placed about 1,200 activists with hidden cameras in Arab polling stations.
tactics.israel: Staff every committee seat and observer slot the law allows in contested and mixed stations. Brief them to report disputes and intimidation to election counsel at once. Keep observers on the count, including the central double-envelope tally where the law allows.

tactics.tactic: Election-day festivals and events near polling stations
tactics.effect: US non-partisan festivals raised turnout 6.5 pp at a 50% baseline in low-salience local elections. There is no high-salience or Israeli estimate.
tactics.israel: Activity near polling stations is regulated, and anything of monetary value to voters carries legal risk. Hold no events, food or entertainment near stations; check with election counsel before any election-day presence there.

tactics.effect: No Israeli causal estimate. In the US, a 1 SD longer trip to the polling place (0.245 mile) cut ballots cast by 2-5%.
tactics.israel: Election-day transport is regulated. In 2019 the CEC chair held that an NGO's plan to bus voters was politically motivated, and that the group had to register as a body active in the elections. Likud has petitioned against the 2026 expat-flight scheme, alleging bribery and a financing-law breach. Do not organise rides. Help supporters plan the trip with free intercity buses and trains, local transport or a family ride, and check with election counsel before any other transport help.

tactics.tactic: Paid media for persuasion (TV, online video)
tactics.effect: Small. In 59 US experiments the average ad moved vote choice about 0.7 pp, not significant. In campaigns' own tests, ads routinely differed by about 50% from the average and theory predicted the winners poorly. Effects fade fast: half-lives of about 4 days in a presidential race and 1-2 days in sub-national races. Ads work through persuasion, not turnout.
tactics.israel: Spend in 21-26 Oct, after testing, and put 10-13% of the budget into tests. Voters move more on information about less-known figures, such as Eisenkot and Yashar's candidates, than on messages about Netanyahu, whom voters already know well. The rescue and insurance creative runs through this channel too.

tactics.effect: Direct vote effect about zero. Across 56 TV debates there was no detectable effect on vote choice. In Italy, candidates canvassing did worse than volunteers.
tactics.israel: The party leader was the main reason for about 19% of voters in 2015 (INES). Use events to recruit volunteers and earn media. Send the right-credentialed leaders (Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman) to persuasion turf, and all leaders to volunteer hubs. Keep visible bloc rallies out of Netanyahu-bloc strongholds, where they can trigger counter-mobilisation.

tactics.tactic: Leaflets, mail, email and digital ads (for turnout)
tactics.effect: Partisan leaflets and mail show no positive effect. GOTV-worded mail gave 0.28 pp per piece in high-salience US races and 0.05 in presidential cycles. Campaign email gave 58.7% turnout against 59.7% in the control group, and purchased Facebook ads showed no effect in two large trials.
tactics.israel: Do not rank turf by the volume of material distributed. Use digital channels to recruit volunteers and relational organisers. Print only a leave-behind with polling-station information.

election_day.title: Chase lagging target stations after each release
election_day.text: The CEC will publish turnout for every regular polling station at least four times during the day, to all lists at once. Before 07:00, give every call-team lead a fixed list of the atlas's positive-value target stations with their 2022 turnout. After each release, rank those stations by how far they trail their locality and their 2022 level, and move callers and relational reminders to the bottom fifth. Never push turnout in stations the atlas scores negative.

election_day.title: Work from pre-election vote plans
election_day.text: On 17 September the High Court barred party representatives at polling stations from telling their parties which identifiable voters have voted. Callers therefore work from supporters identified before election day. They ask whether the supporter has voted yet and help them plan the trip (public transport, a family ride). Election-day transport is regulated, so check with election counsel before offering anything more. The ban hurts machines built on individual tracking most, and Likud has said limits on the Elector app force more manual work.

election_day.title: Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision
election_day.text: The model gives opposite answers under the two objectives. Each 10,000 votes for Ra'am or the Joint List raises the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 seats by about 0.75-0.8 pp, while doing nothing for, or working against, a change-led government. The change bloc runs, funds and brands no turnout work in Arab localities. Any support leadership approves is independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel in writing, with no operational coordination. Arab parties and civil-society groups run their own campaigns. Women and young people are the main upside for Arab turnout, and young Arab voters say they want concrete plans on crime, housing and jobs.

election_day.title: Blunt Likud's use of the releases
election_day.text: Likud plans to use the station releases to rally its base by pointing to high turnout in change-bloc and Arab areas, echoing its 2015 election-day video. Bank identified change-bloc supporters early through private contact (calls, texts, relational asks), with no public turnout claims. Expect the first releases to show high turnout in our areas, and have the counter-message to our own supporters ready before 10:00: the race is close and every vote counts, without naming any group. Do not publish or celebrate turnout in any area.

election_day.title: Get students and young adults home
election_day.text: Voters can vote only at the station of their registered address, and many students and young adults are registered with their parents. Intercity buses on routes over 15 km and all trains are free from 20:00 on 26 Oct until service ends on election day. The announcement does not cover city buses, and Eilat needs advance registration through Egged. Text these supporters the evening before and in the morning with their station address and the last useful train.

election_day.title: Displaced northern and Gaza-border supporters
election_day.text: Between about 40% and 60% of Kiryat Shmona's residents had not returned by September, depending on the report. In the Gaza envelope most evacuees are back, but Be'eri, Nir Oz and Kfar Aza remain largely displaced. In the February 2025 municipal elections, 83 special stations served evacuees from all northern communities; the research found no arrangement yet for the Knesset vote. Confirm the CEC's rules early, then give displaced supporters a trip plan to their station. The atlas halves canvass capacity in these localities. Check any travel help with election counsel.

election_day.title: Observers and lawyers in place
election_day.text: Staff polling committees and observers in contested and mixed stations. In April 2019 a Likud contractor placed about 1,200 activists with hidden cameras in Arab polling stations, so prepare for intimidation complaints. Keep election counsel on call for station disputes and for questions about transport or activity near polling places. Keep observers on the count, including the central double-envelope tally where the law allows.

dos.title: Identify supporters now, contact them in the final ten days
dos.text: Use 11-16 Oct for supporter ID, list cutting and message tests. Live contact works best in the last 7 to 10 days. Effects add up across contacts with no extra synergy, so put repeat contacts where each one is worth most: identified supporters in positive-value turf who are unsure they will vote. Send texts in the 1-3 days before the vote.

dos.title: Work only turf where turnout nets change votes
dos.text: Extra turnout helps only in proportion to the change bloc's lead among the people mobilised. Walk lists come only from positive-value station areas. Field potential combines turnout, persuasion and rescue. In supporter-list ground (Jerusalem, Netanya, Bat Yam, Be'er Sheva, Hadera, Eilat) most of the value is in calls and relational asks to identified supporters, not area canvassing. At 400,000 contacts with 30% of supporters identified, Tel Aviv-Yafo alone yields 530 of the 1,995 net votes.

dos.title: Test before you spend
dos.text: Ads routinely differ by about 50% in effect, and theory predicts the winners poorly. Run rapid online tests of the main frames this week and put 10-13% of the media budget into testing. Leave a random set of target polling stations unworked so the official results show what the field programme achieved.

dos.title: Use right-credentialed messengers in soft-right turf
dos.text: Left-coded messengers can act as a negative cue for right-leaning voters. In Likud-leaning cities and development towns, put Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman, reservists and trusted local figures in front. Parties with a Druze candidate in a winnable slot usually win that candidate's home village, so any Druze work runs through Druze figures on the lists, such as Yashar's Kamil Abu Rokon. The Golan Druze villages and Ghajar are not targeted.

dos.title: Lead persuasion with competence and unity
dos.text: Campaigns move late deciders by raising the salience of issues they own and by building trust in their leaders. Valence messages beat ideology messages in a field test, and priming cooperation raised tolerance across Israeli party lines. Lead with security record, Oct 7 accountability and equal burden. Keep sharper contrast for mobilising the base.

dos.title: Run rescue as insurance media around the final polls
dos.text: Rescue voters are about 2% of a station's voters, so door teams are the wrong channel. Use tested digital and media messages plus calls to identified Blue and White and Reservists supporters, peaking around the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct. Tie the ask to those polls and a clear coalition path.

dos.title: Watch allies near the threshold
dos.text: No change list is near the threshold in the forecast: the Democrats pass in 98% of simulations, Yisrael Beytenu in 97% and Together in 99%. Track this daily. If any falls toward the line, all four lists switch to insurance appeals for it in its strongest localities. In 2022 final polls showed Meretz at 4-5 seats, and it fell below the line as votes concentrated on Yesh Atid.

dos.title: Split turf by lead change list
dos.text: Assign each locality and station to its lead change list, with the runner-up list as second team, and share counts daily so no household is knocked twice. See 'Four lists, one street'.

donts.title: No untargeted turnout work in Netanyahu-bloc strongholds
donts.text: Likud is targeting polling stations where it took about half the vote on about 35% turnout, and values them at 2-3 seats. A joint Likud-RZP programme ranks low-turnout, high-Likud neighbourhoods for door-to-door and phone work. Generic turnout drives there help Likud. Haredi localities turned out at about 75% in 2022, and the atlas projects 92% of their vote to the Netanyahu bloc. The atlas tiers 271 localities as Netanyahu-bloc strongholds. Reach identified supporters there by phone only, and use persuasion in Likud-leaning cities.

donts.title: No change-bloc-run or branded turnout work in Arab localities
donts.text: Visible campaigns about one group's turnout mobilise the other side. Likud's 2019 camera campaign is widely judged to have helped lift Arab turnout from 49% to 59%, though the Joint List's reunification also contributed and the two effects cannot be separated. Likud plans to use high turnout in change-bloc and Arab areas to rally its base this year. Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision; any support is independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel.

donts.title: Do not attack the voters you want to win
donts.text: Coalition voters' support for the judicial overhaul tracked attachment to Netanyahu and hostility to opponents, so attacks that raise hostility harden soft-right voters. Out-group messengers can backfire. Talk to soft Likud voters about competence, repair and fairness, and never mock their 2022 vote.

donts.title: Do not delegitimise Arab voters
donts.text: Most Jewish voters reject a government that relies on Ra'am (57.8% oppose), so in soft-right turf do not build messages around reliance on Ra'am. Lead with competence and a broad government. Never present Arab citizens or their votes as illegitimate. That framing deepens alienation and can depress Arab turnout. The forecast gives the change bloc 61 seats alone in 5.2% of draws, and 18.8% with Ra'am.

donts.title: Do not buy impersonal turnout tools
donts.text: Robocalls, campaign email, purchased social ads and partisan leaflets show turnout effects near zero. Spend that money on volunteer capacity, relational organising and tested persuasion media.

donts.title: Do not run biggest-party appeals against allies
donts.text: Moving votes between Yashar, Together, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu adds no bloc seats. Even a new vote for an average change list is worth only about 1/61,000 of an expected bloc seat, because a seat gained by one change list is sometimes taken from another. In 2022 votes concentrated on the largest opposition list and Meretz fell below the threshold. Within-bloc competition matters only for who gets the mandate, and it must stop if an ally nears the threshold.

donts.title: Do not disparage Reservists or Blue and White voters
donts.text: Reservists-Economic is a right-of-centre, reservist-branded list. Describe its voters with respect and make the message about threshold arithmetic, not about them. The bloc's equal-burden message depends on reservists: 60% of reservists polled would consider not voting for a party that backs a draft exemption, including 48% of right-wing reservists.

donts.title: Do not improvise in legal grey zones
donts.text: Party-organised rides, gifts or anything of monetary value, activity and campaign material near polling stations, sharing the voter register, bulk texting, publishing polls during the blackout and messages based on vote history all carry legal risk. The High Court has banned reporting who voted, and the CEC chair treated an NGO's voter-busing plan as election activity. Check with election counsel before any of these.

messages.who_it_moves: Soft-right and traditional Jewish voters, reservist communities, and centre-right voters still split on prime minister (Netanyahu 44%, Eisenkot 21%, Bennett 20%). Security narrowly leads for Jewish voters (39% vs 38% for the economy, top-two shares) and clearly leads on the right (47%).
messages.frame: Competence and record. Show what the change bloc's leaders did in uniform and in office, and what they will do next. Information about less-known leaders persuades more than attacks on Netanyahu, whom voters already know well. Security-first framing suits localities hit by the war, where a panel study suggests views have moved right (low confidence) and the vote can still go to Yashar or Together.

messages.issue: Oct 7 accountability and a state commission of inquiry
messages.who_it_moves: Soft Likud voters (Oct 7 was the top reason 2022 Likud voters gave for considering a switch, at 37%), secular young voters (decisive for 22%), and the 40% of Netanyahu-bloc voters who say the failures have not been fixed.
messages.frame: Responsibility and repair. A state commission of inquiry is a majority position (55%), and more voters trust an Eisenkot-led government to fix the failures (48% against 30% for Netanyahu). Frame it as fixing what failed for the voter's family and community. Never blame voters for their 2022 choice.

messages.who_it_moves: Reservists and their families (in a December 2024 poll of reservists, 77% said exemptions are no longer affordable and 60% would consider not voting for a party that backs one, including 48% of right-wing reservists), voters in the centre (34% rank the draft in their top two), secular youth (decisive for 26%), and traditional Shas voters in towns such as Kiryat Shmona, Shlomi and Or Yehuda.
messages.frame: Fairness to those who serve. Equal burden for everyone, said by people who served. Avoid hostility to haredim as a group. Do not expect it to move national-religious voters, for whom the draft is the top issue for only 15%. This message depends on the reservist constituency, so rescue messaging to Reservists voters must stay respectful.

messages.who_it_moves: Undecided voters (their top concern, at 25%), voters in the centre (the economy is their leading issue, named by 40.5% in their top two, IDI), including Route 4 commuters, and young voters (25%).
messages.frame: Concrete household costs, such as housing, prices and commuting time. Pair it with credibility, since economic attitudes do not line up with Israeli left and right. Its main use is persuasion and within-bloc choice in Petah Tikva, Holon, Rishon LeZion and Kfar Saba, plus turnout motivation for identified supporters and in positive-value stations.

messages.who_it_moves: Undecided Jewish voters, who emphasised unity and fewer disputes in JPPI's August survey and name polarisation as their second concern (15%) after cost of living; voters in the centre (unity was their top issue at 30% in JPPI's September index); and soft-right voters wary of the opposition.
messages.frame: A broad government that includes the centre-right. In an Israeli experiment, priming cooperation raised tolerance across party lines, while salient competition raises hostility. Use unity framing in persuasion turf and keep sharper contrast for base mobilisation.

messages.issue: Crime and personal safety in Arab society (context; the Democrats' own outreach only)
messages.who_it_moves: Arab voters, especially young people and women, the main sources of potential turnout growth. Crime is the leading issue: 53.5% name it in their top two (IDI) and about 80% rank it first (Statnet). More than 140 people were killed in Arab communities by late June 2026.
messages.frame: Concrete plans on policing, crime and personal safety. Young Arab voters say they want concrete plans on crime, housing and jobs rather than general slogans. The change bloc does not script messages for Arab lists or civil-society groups and runs no turnout messaging in Arab localities. The Democrats, who are touring Arab towns for votes, can carry this frame in their own campaign, transparently and within counsel's rules.

messages.issue: Northern rebuilding and fair treatment of the periphery
messages.who_it_moves: Northern Jewish towns such as Kiryat Shmona, Nahariya, Karmiel, Ma'alot, Tiberias and Shlomi. Across the Haifa and Northern districts (Midgam, April 2026), 65% say the state is abandoning the north, and opposition parties lead 38% to 26% with 27% undecided. Druze towns with planning and Nation-State Law grievances.
messages.frame: Local and practical. Talk about services, rebuilding and jobs, through trusted local figures. Kiryat Shmona's Likud share fell from 58% in 2020 to 49% in 2022, and the Likud-backed mayoral candidate came second in the first round in 2025. In Druze towns the same frame means zoning relief and a freeze on Kaminitz-law enforcement, carried by Druze figures on the lists. In Likud-leaning Jewish towns these are persuasion messages, because generic turnout work there helps Likud. In Druze towns the frame also supports turnout, but their 2026 vote depends on which Druze candidates the lists field.

messages.who_it_moves: Supporters of Blue and White (about 0.6%) and Reservists (about 1.6%), about 90,000 voters at regular polling stations in the atlas, plus voters weighing other small lists.
messages.frame: Make your vote count toward the government you want. In 2022 about 289,000 votes for Meretz and Balad fell below the threshold, Meretz missed by 4,061 votes, and the Netanyahu bloc won 64 seats from a near-tie in votes. Tie the ask to the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct and a clear coalition path. Respect the list, its leader and reservists' service; the message is about the arithmetic, not the voters.

sections.title: What a realistic field programme buys
sections.text: The atlas's planner spends a fixed budget of completed contacts on the best positive-value turf. It leaves out Arab localities and sends door teams only where at least 1,000 contacts are available. Two budgets bracket a realistic programme, 150,000 and 400,000 completed contacts, each run with no supporter lists and with 30% of supporters identified. On those numbers field work is a margin lever worth roughly 1,000 to 2,600 net votes, depending on budget and objective.
bullets: Change-led government: 150,000 contacts buy 935 net votes with no supporter lists and 1,207 with 30% identified (+0.045 and +0.058 points on the chance of a change-led government). 400,000 contacts buy 1,607 and 1,995 (+0.077 and +0.095 points).
Deny Netanyahu 61: 1,541 and 1,739 net votes at 150,000 contacts; 2,290 and 2,638 at 400,000 (+0.09 to +0.16 points).
Change-bloc seats: 1,100 to 2,214 net votes, or 0.02 to 0.04 expected seats. One net vote for an average change list is worth about 1/61,000 of an expected seat.

Saturation (every positive station area at 35% of the roll, plus list programmes) would be worth 3,321 net votes for a change-led government, but it needs about 1.1-1.5 million door conversations. Treat it as a ceiling, not a plan.

Supporter ID pays. At the same budget, identifying 30% of supporters adds about 270-390 net votes for a change-led government and brings Jerusalem, Netanya and Be'er Sheva in through calls to identified supporters. Budget the ID contacts needed to build the lists.
Value is concentrated. At 400,000 contacts with 30% identified, Tel Aviv-Yafo yields 530 net votes, Haifa 134, Jerusalem 83, Ramat Gan 82, Herzliya 74, Netanya 64 and Rishon LeZion 59.

Why it still matters: in 2022 the Netanyahu bloc finished about 30,000 votes ahead, Meretz missed the threshold by 4,061 votes, and in April 2019 New Right missed it by 1,453. Ra'am and RZP-Zehut each pass in about 78% of simulations. Threshold races are decided by margins of this size.

What the numbers leave out: polling-committee and observer coverage, paid media and the rescue media programme. The effect sizes are borrowed from foreign experiments. European canvassing effects are well below US ones, and no Israeli randomised turnout trial exists.

sections.title: Four lists, one street
sections.text: Yashar, Together, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu will canvass the same streets. Moving a vote from one change list to another adds no bloc seats, and a household knocked by two lists is a duplicated contact. Split turf, share counts and keep the doorstep positive.
bullets: Split turf by lead list. The atlas gives each locality and station a lead and a runner-up change list (lead_change_list and second_change_list). The lead list's team works the turf, and the runner-up list supplies a second team where volume justifies it.

Yashar leads in most large target localities, with Together the runner-up across much of the Sharon and Gush Dan and the Democrats runner-up in Tel Aviv-Yafo and Givatayim. Yisrael Beytenu leads in places such as Akko, Nof HaGalil, Qiryat Yam, Arad and Ari'el.

Respect existing splits where they fit the atlas. Yashar is working soft-Likud voters (a pool of about 200,000) and runs a religious-Zionist headquarters covering Gush Etzion, Efrat, Givat Shmuel and Ariel. Yisrael Beytenu has mapped Likud's best stations, including Russian-speaking ex-Likud voters. Yashar launched as a campaign for the Route 4 suburbs.

Share supporter files at the level the law allows. Share the turf map, station assignments and daily counts (doors knocked, supporters identified, vote plans made). Parties may receive the voter register but may not pass it to third parties, so share individual voter records only in a form election counsel has cleared in writing.

No list attacks another list's voters on the doorstep. Partisan contact can demobilise a rival's supporters, and in 2022 votes concentrated on Yesh Atid while Meretz fell below the threshold. Keep within-bloc competition, such as Together's bid to win back ex-Yesh Atid voters from Yashar, to paid media and leaders' messages.
If any ally falls toward the threshold, all four lists switch to insurance messaging for it in its strongest localities.
Druze turf goes to whichever list fields a Druze candidate in a winnable slot, led by that candidate's local figures. The Golan Druze villages and Ghajar are not targeted.
Set a minimum deployment. Door teams go only where at least 1,000 contacts are available; group small targets into one team-day instead of splitting them between lists.

sections.title: Rescue and insurance: a media programme
sections.text: Rescue means persuading supporters of lists likely to miss the 3.25% threshold to vote for a list that will pass. The two targets are Blue and White (about 0.6%, pass chance 1%) and Reservists-Economic (about 1.6%, pass chance 20%). Rescue voters are about 2% of a typical station's voters, so door canvassing is the wrong channel. Run rescue as media, digital and insurance messaging timed around the final published polls on Fri 23 Oct, plus calls to identified voters.
bullets: Channels: tested digital and media creative, and calls and relational asks to identified Blue and White and Reservists supporters. No door teams.

Timing: build creative and call lists from 17 Oct. Peak on Thu 22 and Fri 23 Oct around the final published polls, then keep digital and relational messages running through the weekend on Friday's numbers. No new polls may be published from Sat 24 Oct.

Why polls matter: insurance voting depends on polls showing a list below the threshold and on clear coalition signals. In 2015 Yachad polled 4-5 seats in the final polls and won none; in 2022 Jewish Home polled 1.5-2.2% and won 1.19%.

Size: the atlas assumes, without experimental support, that 5% of contacted voters move, 60% to change lists and 40% to Likud. At saturation that is 286 net votes for a change-led government and 1,014 for change-bloc seats.

Trade-off: under the deny-61 objective rescue is negative (-186 net votes at saturation). Reservists votes would partly go right, and while they stay below the threshold they help deny Netanyahu 61. Leadership decides whether to target Reservists voters at all; Blue and White voters are the cleaner target.

Reservists framing: it is a right-of-centre, reservist-branded list. Use reservists as messengers, respect their service and talk about threshold arithmetic. The bloc's equal-burden message depends on this constituency: 60% of reservists polled would consider not voting for a party that backs a draft exemption, including 48% of right-wing reservists.
Blue and White: a 'withdrawal with honour' is being reported, and the forecast gives it a 0.40 chance. If it happens, offer its voters a respectful next step.
Allies come first. If the Democrats, Yisrael Beytenu or Together slips toward the threshold, insurance messaging turns to protecting that list.

sections.title: Young voters, students and soldiers
sections.text: First-time and young voters are numerous, less certain to vote and often not living where they are registered. Every contact with them starts with the registered address.
bullets: Registration address: voters may vote only at the station of their registered address, which is fixed by a Population Registry cut-off well before the vote (54 days before in 2022). Many students and young adults are registered with their parents, so build each one a trip plan to that station.

Travel: intercity buses on routes over 15 km and all trains are free from 20:00 on Mon 26 Oct until service ends on election day. The announcement does not cover city buses, and Eilat needs advance registration through Egged. Election day is a statutory holiday.

Size and lean: estimates run from about 550,000 (Midgam) to about 640,000 (CBS, via IDI) first-time voters. Among Jewish first-time voters Midgam found Yashar 16%, Likud 14%, Together 10%, the Democrats 7%, Yisrael Beytenu 6% and 10% undecided, and 74% place themselves right or centre-right.

Certainty: in a Dialog poll of 18-22-year-olds, 67% were certain to vote (71% of Jewish and 53% of Arab youth), and 14% were undecided on party (20% of young women, 8% of young men). Draft policy was decisive for 26% of secular youth and the Oct 7 inquiry for 22%.
Campuses: recruit volunteers and relational organisers, run vote-plan conversations and record where each student is registered. Friend-to-friend texting had large turnout effects in a US trial.
Families: a text to a young voter reaches housemates (about 30% spillover) but not parents living elsewhere, so contact parents separately.

Soldiers: soldiers away from home vote by double envelope, the largest group of envelope voters, and their ballots are counted centrally after the regular count. Treat military bases as off-limits for campaigning and reach soldiers through family and friends; check with election counsel.
Why it lasts: voting once raises the chance of voting in a later election by about 10 points, and the forecast gives a repeat election a 41.9% chance.

sections.title: The Arab-sector decision for leadership
sections.text: Whether the change bloc puts any resources into Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, not a field-team one. The model gives opposite answers under the two objectives. Whatever leadership decides, the change bloc runs, funds and brands no turnout work in Arab localities, and any support is independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel. This analysis is for internal use.
bullets: The trade-off: per 10,000 extra votes, Ra'am adds -0.04 points and the Joint List -0.41 points to the chance of a change-led government, but +0.82 and +0.75 points to the chance of denying Netanyahu 61. In the formation model these votes turn Netanyahu-bloc wins into deadlock while diluting change-list seats.

Under the change-led-government objective the model recommends no investment. If leadership puts weight on blocking, the model favours Ra'am-majority areas over Joint List areas, since Ra'am votes score better under both objectives.
Context: the change bloc reaches 61 seats alone in 5.2% of forecast draws and in 18.8% with Ra'am. The Netanyahu bloc reaches 61 in 21.7%.

Rules: no change-bloc-run, funded or branded turnout work in Arab localities, and no operational coordination with Arab parties or civil-society groups. Coordination can turn an outside group's turnout work into regulated election activity: in 2019 the CEC chair required an NGO busing voters to register as a body active in the elections. Any support leadership approves needs written clearance from election counsel.

Why branding backfires: Likud's 2019 camera campaign is widely judged to have helped lift Arab turnout from 49% to 59%, though the Joint List's reunification also contributed. Likud plans to use the station turnout releases to point to high turnout in change-bloc and Arab areas.

Arab lists are independent and are not members of the bloc. The Democrats' own campaign for Arab votes, including tours of Arab towns and Arabic social media, is that list's decision under the same transparent, counsel-cleared rules.

For leadership's information: Arab turnout was 53.2% in 2022, and scenario polling links the configuration now running (a three-party Joint List and a separate Ra'am) to about 59%. Crime is the leading issue, and women and young people are the main upside. Rhetoric that paints reliance on Arab parties as illegitimate can depress turnout.

Language: never describe Arab or Druze towns as change-bloc turf or majorities. The atlas tiers Arab localities as Arab-list turf under every objective and leaves them out of the field planner. Keep town-level values for Arab localities out of shareable material.

sections.title: Legal guardrails
sections.text: Election-day transport, gifts, campaign activity near polling stations and the publication of polls are regulated under Israeli election law. The points below are what the research found; they are not legal advice. For anything else, check with election counsel before acting, and keep a written log of clearances.
bullets: Who has voted: on 17 Sep 2026 the High Court barred party representatives at polling stations from telling their parties which identifiable voters have voted, citing election law and privacy law. Parties may still urge people to vote.
Station turnout: the CEC will publish aggregate turnout for every regular station at least four times on election day, to all lists at once and with no names.

Voter data: parties receive the voter register but may not pass it to third parties. Sharing voter-level data between lists, with outside groups or with vendors needs written clearance. Whether vote-history data may be used before election day is unclear, so send no message that refers to a voter's own past turnout without clearance.

Transport: election-day transport is regulated. In 2019 the CEC chair held that an NGO's plan to bus voters was politically motivated and that the group had to register as a body active in the elections. Likud has challenged the 2026 expat-flight scheme as bribery and a financing breach. No party-organised rides; check with election counsel before any transport help.
Gifts and benefits: anything of monetary value to voters is regulated. Check with election counsel before offering food, travel or any service.

Near polling stations: campaign propaganda and activity near polling stations are regulated. Clear any presence, material, event or food near stations with counsel, and brief committee members and observers on their role.
Polls: final polls may be published until the end of Fri 23 Oct. From Sat 24 Oct to the close of polls, publish, post or leak no poll, including internal ones. Confirm the exact cut-off with counsel.
Outside groups: coordinating with an NGO or civil-society group can make its work regulated election activity and raise party-financing questions. Clear any joint activity with counsel first.
Bulk messaging and privacy: check the rules on bulk texts and calls with counsel before the final-week waves.
